title: Dedicated Burst option — packaging + pricing coordination (Finance/Sales/Legal)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
Goal
Coordinate pricing + packaging inputs for the Dedicated “Burst Capacity” add-on across Finance, Sales/CS, and Legal. Produce a GA-ready recommendation (tiers, limits, billing line items, and contract language hooks) aligned with platform guardrails and metering accuracy.

Context
Dedicated customers want temporary throughput increases for predictable peaks without resizing their baseline reservation. Product is proposing Redwood-managed shared burst pools (segmented by region/hardware class) with strict admission control and fleet safety caps. Packaging needs to make (a) what is guaranteed vs best-effort explicit and (b) billable units auditable and reconcilable.

Deliverable(s)
1) GA packaging summary for Sales/CS (what to sell, when to recommend, and what not to promise)
2) Pricing bands + approval notes from Finance (including constraints/conditions)
3) Legal-approved contract/SLA language stub (definitions + disclaimers)
4) Billing/metering requirements for Engineering (line items, rounding, idempotency expectations)

Proposed packaging (v2 — for approval)
Add-on: “Dedicated Burst Capacity”
- Eligibility: Dedicated customers only; burst enabled per tenant + per region/hardware class.
- Customer-facing behavior: When baseline dedicated allocation is fully utilized, eligible requests may borrow from burst pools up to configured caps; when burst denied, customer sees deterministic denial reason codes and receives backpressure/429 per existing overload semantics.
- Non-goal: No cross-region bursting in v1; no customer-specific pools in v1.

Tiers (commercial packaging)
- Burst Standard
  - Max burst ratio: up to 1.5x baseline GPU allocation per region/hardware class (subject to fleet safety caps)
  - Monthly burst spend cap: configurable (default set in order form)
  - Priority: standard
- Burst Priority (Enterprise)
  - Max burst ratio: up to 2.0x baseline (subject to fleet safety caps)
  - Priority tier: “gold” (admission controller priority tiering, anti-starvation constraints)
  - Requires: SRE review of neighbor-risk + capacity availability in target region/hardware

Billing & metering proposal (requires ENG alignment)
- Billable unit: burst GPU-seconds (or GPU-minutes) consumed above baseline dedicated allocation
- Billing line item: “Dedicated Burst Usage (GPU-seconds)” with region + hardware class breakdown available in reporting export
- Rounding: aggregate at 1-minute granularity per tenant per region/hardware class (avoid per-request micro-rounding)
- Idempotency: enforce idempotency keys on retry paths to prevent double counting
- Reconciliation: monthly reconciliation report export must match billing pipeline totals within agreed tolerance; any drift triggers Finance/SRE review

Guardrail / SLO packaging notes (must be explicit in contract + enablement)
- Burst is best-effort and subject to admission control, pool availability, and global fleet safety circuit breakers.
- Dedicated baseline SLA remains in effect for baseline capacity; burst capacity itself is not capacity-reserved.
- Platform will protect non-burst tenants; Redwood may throttle/deny burst to preserve fleet SLOs.

Target GA stance for Sales
- “You can burst above baseline, but it’s controlled and may be denied; you will always get clear denial reasons and dashboards to see what happened.”
- “Burst is a cost lever and a peak-handling lever, not a replacement for chronic under-provisioning.”

References
- Confluence packaging draft: sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-burst-option-packaging.json
- Finance sensitivity model: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance-and-legal/burst-capacity-unit-economics-sensitivity.json
- Contract language thread: sources/gmail/michael_grant/20250301-burst-capacity-contract-language.json
- Engineering metering ticket: ENG-4827

Owner checklist
- [x] Align on billable unit + rounding + reconciliation requirements (Finance + Eng)
- [x] Confirm what Sales can promise at GA (enablement + standard objections)
- [x] Confirm contract definitions, SLA carveouts, and audit log commitments (Legal + Security)
- [x] Document approval conditions and any launch gates (Finance + SRE)
acceptance_criteria:
- Finance approval obtained (pricing bands + margin guardrails documented) with any conditions captured for GA.
- Legal-approved language stub produced: definitions of Burst Capacity, availability/best-effort, limits, throttling/denial, and reporting.
- Sales enablement one-pager updated to match final packaging (no promises that contradict admission control / circuit breaker behavior).
- Engineering has a clear metering spec: billable unit, rounding, idempotency on retries, reconciliation expectations, and reporting surface.
- Open questions below are resolved OR explicitly deferred with an owner/date.
open_questions:
1) Price metric: Do we anchor burst usage to GPU-seconds only, or do we also provide an optional token-based view for customer comprehension? (Finance prefers GPU-seconds for cost alignment; Sales prefers token framing.)
2) Minimum commit: Is burst purely pay-as-you-go, or do we require a small monthly minimum add-on for Priority tier to reduce “free option” behavior? (Finance request.)
3) Cap defaults: What are default monthly caps and max burst ratios per tier that minimize surprise bills while still being useful? (Need CS input.)
4) SLA language: Do we explicitly exclude burst from any latency SLA, or do we promise “no worse than baseline” when burst is granted? (SRE strongly prefers exclusion; Product prefers simple wording.)
5) Credits/Trials: Do we offer a burst trial (time-boxed) for Dedicated customers upgrading? If yes, how do we prevent it from skewing pool sizing assumptions? (Sales request.)
6) Overages: When the spend cap is reached, do we hard deny burst or allow “soft” overages requiring explicit customer opt-in? (Billing/CS workflow.)
decisions:
Final decisions captured for GA (as of 2025-03-01)
- Billing unit: GPU-seconds above baseline (aggregated to 1-minute buckets) with per region/hardware class breakdown available in reporting.
- Commercial tiers: Standard + Priority. Priority includes higher max burst ratio and priority tiering in admission control (subject to anti-starvation constraints).
- Contract stance: Burst is best-effort; Redwood may deny/throttle burst to preserve fleet safety and non-burst tenant SLOs. Baseline Dedicated SLA unaffected.
- Caps: Default monthly spend cap required on order form; customer may request higher caps via approval (Finance + SRE signoff for Priority).
- Trials: Limited trial allowed only with explicit pool capacity review in target region/hardware; must be time-boxed and include a conservative cap.

- Product owner: Confirmed 2025-02-24 by Lauren Bishop.
